answer_1.quote: In this paper, our aim is to mitigate this problem in LLM-based MT by optimizing the model toward a preference for better word alignment.
answer_1.outputs: The paper focuses on improving machine translation outputs by mitigating hallucination and omission through word alignment preferences.

answer_2.quote: We utilize DPO in this work due to the ease of use and effectiveness.

answer_3.quote: We use one of the most powerful LLM, gpt-4-0613, as an evaluator. LLM is prompted to check whether the given translation has hallucination or omission referring to the given source texts.
methods: direct evaluation with coverage score prediction
prompt-based assessment of hallucination and omission

answer_4.quote: Three volunteers who speak Chinese and English are asked to assess the quality of the translation and the degree of hallucination and omission for the baseline and our model, without knowing which model generates the translations.
answer_4.guideline: Assess the quality of the translation and the degree of hallucination and omission.
